headline: Under 2026 tax-benefit rules the paper's result holds where computable — a revenue-neutral in-work transfer still beats a demogrant (Ψ_w < Ψ_d) in 8 of 10 countries with a well-defined trade-off — but bottom-quintile participation tax rates have diverged sharply, falling 24 pp in Denmark while rising 40+ pp in Spain and Italy as they built minimum-income floors.

notes: Policy-rules-only update: the paper's 1998 cell weights and formulas are held fixed; only EUROMOD tax-benefit rules change (J2.54+ beta), on hypothetical households, 14 countries, 2009-2026. UK out of scope.

Central finding and caveat: bottom-decile PTRs/MTRs now approach 100% in single-earner hypothetical households (genuine traps), which destabilises the paper's closed-form Ψ (it divides by 1-rate). Ψ is reported only for the 10 'stable' countries; the robust results are the decile PTR profiles and the bottom-quintile PTR change.
V4 (q=0, no-UB panel) is the headline because 7 of 14 countries triggered no meaningful unemployment benefit in the hypothetical households (pre-declared rule).

Strict OECD level-validation holds for singles (set V = {DK, FR}); lone-parent and two-earner cells diverge. The headline is a CHANGE, so country-constant offsets cancel and gate 3b validates the change for V_Δ (6 countries).

Not executed (cut to protect the headline + all six gates): variants V3 (dispersion), V5 (rent=20% AW), V6 (one child), lhw=40, employer-SSC inversion. V1 (CTR fixed) computed and leaves the headline unchanged.
Data fix: staged earn_nt_net 2024 values were monthly not annual (corrected); 2026 AW uprated by the XML $f_yem index.
